content_units: Allergy Relief Options at a Glance

For mild seasonal allergy symptoms with nasal congestion and no fever, the best fit is usually a   low-drowsiness oral antihistamine plus saline spray if needed for congestion  . Because driving is important, options with the   lowest sedation risk   are more favorable.
Pros and Cons Comparison Table
Option   Best for   Pros   Cons

Cetirizine 10 mg once daily     Sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes, general allergy relief   Often works well for common allergy symptoms; once-daily dosing; available OTC     More likely to cause drowsiness   than loratadine in some people; may impair alertness for driving; may not fully relieve congestion by itself

Loratadine 10 mg once daily     Daytime allergy relief when low drowsiness matters     Usually less sedating  ; once daily; good for sneezing, runny nose, itchy/watery eyes; better suited for people who drive   May feel a little less effective than cetirizine for some people; may not fully relieve nasal congestion alone

Saline nasal spray as needed     Nasal dryness, stuffiness, mucus, mild congestion     Non-drowsy  ; can be used alongside either antihistamine; helps moisturize and loosen mucus; no known drug-allergy concern in this scenario   Short-term symptom relief only; does not treat the allergy response itself; may need repeated use during the day
Best Fit for Low-Drowsiness Driving Days
Most practical starting choice:     Loratadine 10 mg once daily
- Best match when   low drowsiness   is a priority.
- Add   saline nasal spray as needed   for congestion support.
- If trying   cetirizine  , use extra caution the first time because some people feel sleepy even at standard doses.
When Medical Advice Makes Sense
Seek medical advice if symptoms last   more than 14 days  , or sooner if any of these happen:
- Symptoms are   getting worse instead of improving
- Nasal congestion becomes severe or you develop   sinus pain/pressure
- You develop   fever
- Mucus becomes thick, foul-smelling, or significantly discolored for several days
- You have   wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness  , or coughing fits
- Drowsiness from medicine affects   driving or work safety
- Symptoms are frequent enough that you need a better long-term allergy plan
Practical Use Notes
- Try only   one oral antihistamine at a time   unless a clinician advises otherwise.
- For daytime use and commuting,   loratadine is usually the safer first OTC pick  .
-   Saline spray   can be used with either option because it does not add sedation.
